title: Burning Bonds and Nurse Car Costs
summary:
*   **Financial Housekeeping:** City officials publicly incinerated $417,000 worth of various municipal bonds (including refunding, water works, and sewer bonds) in the City Hall furnace.
*   **Property Tax Correction:** Approved the cancellation of $100 in excessive property assessments for two lots in the Welch Subdivision, instructing the assessor to provide credits.
*   **Public Health Support:** Allocated $135 to the Municipal Nurse to cover car expenses like gasoline and oil, aiding her in city service.
*   **Infrastructure Compensation:** Authorized a $3,000 payment as a "profit fee" to the contractors, Potts, Moore & Prentice, for their work on the city's sewage disposal plant.

SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL: Austin, Texas, Apr. 4, 1919.

The Council met with all members present.
There was laid before the Council the following resolution: Whereas, 62x220 feet out of
the northwest corner and Mrs. Annie C. McNair : 59¾x220 feet out of the southeast corner

Now, therefore,
BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AUSTIN, TEXAS: That the assessment fixed
against said 62x220 feet out of the northwest corner and also the assessment against the
said 59¾x220 feet out of the southeast corner of Lot No. 4, Block No. 4, Outlot 34/46,
Division "O" of Welch's Subdivision be cancelled as excessive, and the Assessor and
Collector is hereby instructed to make credits on the assessment of said special pieces of
property in accordance with the terms of this resolution.
The resolution was adopted by a vote of 5 yeas, no nays.

Austin, Texas, April 9, 1919.

The Council met with all members present.
The Mayor laid before the Council the following resolution: RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL
OF THE CITY OF AUSTIN: That One Hundred and Thirty-five Dollars ($135.00) or so much
thereof as may prove to be necessary be and the same is hereby appropriated out of the
General Contingent Fund of the City of Austin to be paid to the Municipal Nurse at the
rate of Fifteen Dollars ($15.00) per month to pay for the use of gasoline, lubricating oil
and other incidentals in and about her automobile used in the service of the City as
Municipal Nurse.
The resolution was adopted by a vote of 5 yeas, no nays.
APPROVED, Apr. 9, 1919: A. P. Wooldridge, Mayor.

Prentice, Contractors for the sewage disposal plant for this City, have been reimbursed
for an amount for material, supplies and labor according to contract expended on account
of the construction of the sewage disposal plant in the amount of Thirty-five Thousand
Forty-five Dollars and Eighty Cents ($35,045.80); and Whereas, said Potts, Moore &
Prentice have not been paid any profit fee for and upon their disbursement of said
Thirtyfive Thousand Forty-five Dollars and Eighty Cents ($35,045.80). Now, therefore,
